about: The committed matrix of docs/upstream-parity.md (decision D6): each cell holds an image of wz to the original built by this repository, with the verdict of decision D1 (WIN, TIE or LOSS; only WIN counts). The rows of a run are the output of `scripts/lib/kit_compare.py --format rows` for that run, never figures copied by hand; a change that moves a cell moves its run here, in the same commit, with the run that measured it.

runs.target: mcu-zephyr: the T2G kit (CYT4BF, Cortex-M7 at 350 MHz) on its own Ethernet to a zenohd 1.10.0 with its REST plugin on the bench host
runs.workload: W1: answer the two GETs of the wz client's keys, 2,000 times each per boot, through the router
runs.method: scripts/kit-lane.sh compare --boots 12, compare builds (CONFIG_WZ_MEMORY_REPORT), images alternated per round, turnaround read at the host's wire
runs.reference: zephyr-pico-queryable-st: zenoh-pico with the wz client's planes (queryable, UDP unicast) in its single-threaded arm, the stronger of its two arms in every cell of this run
runs.tree: origin's main at 09b20b7ff4 with the SCE pin at 98803c0bc8 (ADR 0073, a machine built under a session id proven when it is compiled; ADR 0074, the engine's per-turn state in its shared core; ADR 0075, a machine keeps a delayed-send queue and a donedata slot only when its document fills them), the heap client as the fixed client's code with its storage block taken from the kernel heap at start, the session negotiating a batch of 1,024 bytes (CONFIG_WZ_BATCH_BYTES), replies of at most 96 bytes and the session machine's queues declared at 16 events; sent to the bench host
caveats: Two programs written for one workload, the same keys, bodies and encoding on the wire (decision D4): the cells move to pico's own programs on both libraries when the pico C ABI runs on the MCU (step M5).

The ram cell holds each image's static RAM, which includes the kernel heap pool each image is configured with (128 KiB for pico and for the wz heap client); the smallest pool each image runs in is not measured yet, so a ram WIN against pico is not yet a claim.

Both sides of this run poll the receive path out of the ITCM (CONFIG_WZ_POLL_PATH_IN_ITCM). The turnaround of the fixed client reads 0.1945 ms and the heap client's 0.1950 against 0.2027 for the single-threaded pico: the ratios, 0.9600 (interval 0.9292 to 0.9874) and 0.9624 (0.9311 to 0.9904), twelve boots of each image, are what holds. The upper end of the heap client's interval is 0.96 percent under 1.

The text cells are of the compare builds, which carry the memory report: the fixed client reads 143,772 bytes here and 142,672 in the build the kit lane's text gate holds (deploy/text_budget.json), 1,100 more; the heap client 143,712 against 142,620. The reference reads 144,836 bytes as in the run before.

The stack_used cell is the difference of two sums of thread readings, and only the difference is the cell's. The heap client reads 5,652 against 5,692, 40 bytes (0.7 percent) under; the fixed client reads 5,668, 24 bytes (0.4 percent) under: its receive queue thread of the network stack reads 512 bytes where the heap client's reads 496, and its main thread reads 2,720 in both (the receive of a handshake message, not a query's answer). That thread is Zephyr's, and why its reading differs between two builds of one code was not examined.

The heap_peak cell of the heap client is its storage block, 8,384 bytes, taken from the kernel heap at start, and the allocator's own 28: 8,412 bytes against the reference's 9,280. The block was 11,568 bytes before the batch, the reply limit, the queues and the delayed-send queues of the two machines were stated by what the client carries (a batch of 1,024 bytes and replies of 96 are this firmware's numbers: the documents it answers with are 63 and 72 bytes, and a router takes the smaller of its batch and the node's).

The margins are small: text 1,064 bytes (0.73 percent) for the fixed client and 1,124 (0.78) for the heap client, flash 1,160 and 1,220, stack_used 24 and 40 bytes under the reference. Text and flash are of deterministic builds, so they hold until a change moves them; a change is read against these margins and not against the verdict.

The text and the instruction-cache layout move together on this kit: the same source read 41.4 and 42.0 us in the stamps with 392 bytes of unreached code between them, so a turnaround difference below a microsecond is not attributed to a source change.
